ROC: Rate of climb. The vertical speed of an aircraft expressed in feet per minute (ft/min) or metres per second (m/s), indicating how rapidly the aircraft gains altitude.
ROD: Rate of descent. The vertical speed of an aircraft expressed in feet per minute (ft/min) or metres per second (m/s), indicating how rapidly the aircraft loses altitude.
ROL: Remote online. Used in NOTAM text to indicate that a system, service, or facility is accessible or operated via remote online connection rather than on-site presence.
ROTA: Runway occupancy time and arrival. An ATC metric measuring the time an arriving aircraft spends on the runway from touchdown to vacating, used for runway capacity analysis and sequencing efficiency.
RP: Reference point. A specified geographical location used as a basis for navigation, reporting, or measurement in aviation operations and NOTAM text.
RPA: Remotely piloted aircraft. An unmanned aircraft controlled from a remote pilot station, operating under the oversight of a licensed remote pilot-in-command.
RPAS: Remotely piloted aircraft system. The complete system comprising a remotely piloted aircraft, its remote pilot station, control links, and any associated equipment required for flight operations.
RPI: Runway point of intersection. A defined point on the runway where two runways or a runway and a taxiway intersect, used for position reporting and surface movement coordination.
RPL: Repetitive flight plan. A pre-established flight plan filed for a series of regularly scheduled identical flights, stored in the ATS system for automatic activation without requiring individual submission each time.
RPO: Runway point of origin. The designated starting point of a runway, typically the runway threshold, used as a reference for distance measurements and position reporting along the runway.
RPS: Radar position symbol. A graphical symbol displayed on an ATC radar screen representing the position of an aircraft or vehicle, including its track and identity information.
RQMN: Requirement. Used in NOTAM text and aviation documentation to indicate a necessary condition, specification, or criterion that must be met for a procedure or operation.
RQP: Request flight plan. A message or action requesting the submission or activation of a flight plan, typically used in coordination between ATC units or flight planning facilities.
RQST: Request. Used in NOTAM text and aviation communications to indicate a demand or solicitation for information, clearance, service, or action.
RRC: Rescue radio channel. A dedicated radio frequency assigned for use by search and rescue (SAR) operations, providing communication between rescue units and coordinating agencies.
RSC: Runway surface condition. A report describing the state of the runway surface, including contaminants such as water, snow, slush, ice, or debris, used by pilots to assess braking action and landing performance.
RSR: En route surveillance radar. A long-range ground-based radar system used by ATC for monitoring aircraft along established airways and en route segments, typically covering extended ranges beyond terminal airspace.
RST: Reinstate or reinstated. Used in NOTAM text to indicate that a facility, service, or condition has been restored to its normal operating status after being out of service or degraded.
RSU: Runway supervision unit. The ATC or airport operations unit responsible for monitoring runway activity, conducting safety inspections, and coordinating runway maintenance and usage.
RTD: Delayed (runway throughput). Used in NOTAM text to indicate a delay in runway operations that reduces the rate of arrivals and departures, affecting overall airport throughput capacity.
RTHL: Runway threshold lights. A row of green lights installed across the runway threshold to mark the beginning of the landing surface, providing visual guidance to pilots on final approach.
RTN: Return. Used in NOTAM text and aviation communications to indicate a movement back to a previous location, position, or condition.
RTO: Rejected take-off. A high-speed aborted take-off initiated by the pilot due to an engine failure, system malfunction, or other safety concern, requiring maximum braking and deceleration within the remaining runway distance.
RTS: Return to service. Used in NOTAM and maintenance reports to indicate that a facility, system, or piece of equipment has been restored to operational status after maintenance, repair, or inspection.
RTZL: Runway touchdown zone lights. A series of white light bars embedded in the runway surface within the touchdown zone, providing visual identification of the designated landing area for pilots during approach and landing.
RUT: Standard route. A pre-defined, published route used for air traffic flow management, ensuring consistent and efficient routing of aircraft between specified points or airspace sectors.
RV: Rescue vessel. A watercraft designated and equipped for search and rescue (SAR) operations, capable of recovering personnel from water in the event of an aviation ditching or emergency.
RVC: Runway visual range (converted). A calculated RVR value derived from transmissometer measurements and converted using standard algorithms, representing the horizontal visibility along the runway for operational use.
RVI: Runway visual range (touchdown). The RVR measurement specifically at the touchdown zone of the runway, used by pilots as the primary visibility reference for approach and landing operations.
RVR: Runway visual range. The horizontal distance a pilot can see along the runway surface from the approach end, measured by automated sensors and used to determine whether landing or take-off minima are met in low-visibility conditions.
RVT: Runway visual range (all). A composite RVR value representing measurements from multiple points along the runway (touchdown, midpoint, and rollout), providing an overall visibility assessment for the full runway length.
RVV: Runway visibility value. A visibility measurement reported when RVR equipment is not available, representing the prevailing visibility along the runway expressed in metres or statute miles.
RWY: Runway. A defined rectangular surface on an aerodrome prepared for the landing and take-off of aircraft, identified by its magnetic orientation number and used as the primary operating surface for flight operations.
RXA: Reception. Used in aviation communications and NOTAM text to refer to the quality, availability, or status of radio signal reception between aircraft and ground stations.
S: South. The cardinal direction opposite north, used in aviation for navigation, runway designation, wind direction reporting, and airspace classification references.
SA: Sand. An ICAO meteorological code used in NOTAM text and weather reports to indicate sand as a surface contaminant or a weather phenomenon (e.g., blowing sand) that may affect visibility and operations.
SAE: Safe aircraft and engine. A status designation indicating that an aircraft and its engine(s) have been inspected and confirmed to meet safety standards for continued flight operations.
SAR: Search and rescue. The coordinated effort to locate and assist persons in distress or imminent danger, encompassing aviation SAR operations involving aircraft, ground teams, and maritime vessels coordinated by a Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC).
SAT: Satellite. Used in NOTAM text and aviation communications to refer to satellite-based systems, including satellite navigation (GNSS), satellite communications (SATCOM), and satellite-based augmentation systems (SBAS).
SATCOM: Satellite communication. Voice and data communication between aircraft and ground stations relayed via satellite networks, enabling global connectivity beyond the range of terrestrial VHF/HF radio.
SB: Southbound. A direction of flight or traffic flow proceeding toward the south, used in flight planning, ATC routing, and NOTAM text.
SBY: Stand by. Used in aviation communications and NOTAM text to instruct a pause or to indicate that a system or facility is in a standby mode, ready for activation when required.
SC: Stratocumulus. An ICAO cloud classification describing a low-level cloud type composed of grey or whitish patches, rolls, or rounded masses, often covering large portions of the sky and associated with stable atmospheric conditions.
SCT: Scattered (3/8 to 4/8 cloud cover). An ICAO cloud coverage code indicating that clouds cover between 3/8 and 4/8 of the sky, representing broken to nearly half-covered sky conditions.
SDF: Step-down fix. A defined navigation point on an instrument approach procedure where a lower minimum altitude is authorized, allowing the aircraft to descend to a lower altitude after passing the fix while maintaining obstacle clearance.
SE: South-east. The intercardinal direction midway between south and east, used in aviation for navigation, wind direction, and airspace referencing.
SEB: South-eastbound. A direction of flight or traffic flow proceeding toward the south-east, used in flight planning, ATC routing, and NOTAM text.
SEC: Second(s). A unit of time equal to 1/60 of a minute, used in aviation for timing procedures, separation standards, and operational intervals.
SEP: September. The ninth month of the Gregorian calendar, used in aviation date notation and NOTAM validity periods.
SER: Service or servicing. Used in NOTAM text and maintenance reports to indicate the provision of maintenance, support, or operational availability of a facility, system, or piece of equipment.
SEV: Severe. Used in NOTAM text and meteorological reports to indicate an intense or extreme condition, such as severe turbulence, severe icing, or severe weather phenomena, requiring heightened pilot awareness.
